comments.body:
PLAN REVIEW #1 (at HEAD e1566b5f4): BLOCK, 4 findings. All four were REAL defects in the plan, not
gate noise. Remediated:

1. COH/E1 — SELF-CONTRADICTING AC. AC7 demanded docs/env-vars.md 'regenerates with no diff', while the
   Approach introduces NINE new env vars (REBAR_LLM_{FRONTIER,STANDARD,TRIVIAL}_{MODEL,PROVIDER,
   ENDPOINT}) that necessarily appear in the generator's output — and Scope named only config.py and
   tests/. The AC could not be satisfied by a correct implementation. Scope now names docs/env-vars.md
   as a deliverable, and the AC now says the file is REGENERATED AND COMMITTED here, lists the nine
   vars, and THEN re-running the generator is a no-op — which is what the drift gate actually checks.

2. E4 — I DESCRIBED UNBUILT WORK AS SHIPPED. The plan said an environment needing a fallback chain
   uses REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE 'which exists for exactly this'. It does not exist anywhere in src/ or
   docs/ — it is sibling task cb6f's deliverable. Present tense for a sibling's unlanded work is a
   trap for an executor who would go looking for it. Now stated explicitly as NOT existing yet, with
   the consequence spelled out: until cb6f lands there is no environment-only way to set a fallback
   chain, and that is accepted because this ticket's job is the SCHEMA, not the delivery mechanism.

3+4. T8/E2 — THE FALLBACK SUB-OBJECT SCHEMA WAS NEVER DEFINED. 'An array of sub-objects' is not a
   spec; nobody could write the parser or a test against it. Now a decided table: a fallback entry is
   a provider target with exactly a class slot's fields MINUS fallback — model (required), provider
   (optional -> infer_provider), endpoint (optional), api_key FORBIDDEN.

   DECIDED: it is NON-RECURSIVE. An entry carrying its own fallback key is a typed config error. The
   chain is already an ordered list, so nesting adds no expressiveness while introducing cycle risk
   and unbounded resolution depth. Also pinned: fallback = [] and an absent fallback key are the SAME
   thing (no fallbacks), so the empty-array case cannot be read two ways.

Four ACs added, each falsifiable: api_key rejected on an ENTRY (not just a slot), nested fallback
rejected, entry-level provider inference matching slot behaviour, and the corrected doc-regeneration
criterion. Re-review running.

comments.body:
IMPLEMENTED AND VERIFIED. Gerrit change 1102, commit 18dda0f27, LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1.

src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py, 178 LOC. config.py UNTOUCHED at 777 (the one-way import edge holds:
model_classes imports infer_provider/DEFAULT_MODEL/VERIFIER_DEFAULT_MODEL from config; config does
not import it back).

HELD-OUT TDD. 16 tests authored before the code; ONE (the happy path) given to the implementer, the
other 15 physically removed from the worktree. All 15 passed on the implementer's FIRST attempt.
Then six behavioural mutations, each asserted-as-applied before the red check:

  frontier default -> sonnet ................................. CAUGHT
  skip the api_key check on fallback ENTRIES ................. CAUGHT
  allow a NESTED fallback .................................... CAUGHT
  env override clobbers sibling fields ....................... CAUGHT
  double-prefix an already-qualified model ................... CAUGHT
  unknown class silently defaults instead of raising ......... CAUGHT

Suite: 8175 passed, 74 skipped, 0 failed (0:26:31) — the prior 8159 plus exactly these 16.

ONE DEFECT THE BEHAVIOURAL ORACLE COULD NOT CATCH, worth recording as the lesson from this ticket.
docs/env-vars.md is DERIVED: scripts/gen_env_registry.py scans src/rebar for LITERAL env-var name
strings and CI fails the build if the committed copy drifts. The first implementation built the nine
names with an f-string, which is fine Python but INVISIBLE to the scanner — regenerating produced
only 'model_classes.py:83 — os.environ.get(<non-literal>)', filing the nine vars under 'name not
statically determinable' instead of documenting them. 16/16 tests passed and six mutations were
caught, and the change would STILL have failed CI. Structural constraints (module size, derived-file
regeneration) live outside the behavioural net; that is why they belong in the implementer brief. I
briefed module size and missed the doc generator — one round-trip.

Fixed by spelling the nine names out as literals, with a comment saying WHY so nobody tidies it back
into an f-string. Verified properly: the nine now appear attributed to model_classes.py, the
<non-literal> line is gone, and REGENERATING PRODUCES BYTE-IDENTICAL OUTPUT (my first idempotency
check was wrong — I diffed against HEAD, which of course differs by the nine new rows; the real
check is snapshot-then-regenerate-then-compare).

THREE UNDER-SPECIFICATIONS the implementer flagged, resolved here so cc33 does not re-litigate them:
1. A slot present but with model missing/empty falls back to the class default rather than erroring.
   Erroring would force every configured slot to repeat model even when it only wants to set provider.
2. A bare model whose provider cannot be inferred is returned UNPREFIXED, mirroring the existing
   _pai_model precedent in anthropic_model.py. Same as today's behaviour, so no existing config moves.
3. An empty-string env var is treated as UNSET (falls through to table/default), matching the rest of
   rebar's env layer.

PLAN REVIEW #2 (post-scope-correction): BLOCK, 2 findings, same root cause — and a direct
consequence of MY OWN scope narrowing, so worth recording rather than just fixing.

When I found llm/config.py at 777 of the 800 cap I redirected the schema to a new model_classes.py
and restricted config.py to 'only the env docstring'. That fixed the size problem and created a new
one: nothing then named WHO extracts the model_classes sub-table from the loaded config and passes
it to parse_class_slots. The parser took an already-loaded mapping, so with no named caller the
schema was UNREACHABLE FROM REAL CONFIGURATION — a parser nothing calls, which every downstream
consumer (172e, 7761, cc33) would have had to re-invent. Both findings say this; the reviewer was
right and I had introduced the gap two reviews earlier.

RESOLVED: load_class_slots(repo_root=None) in model_classes.py —

    return parse_class_slots(_read_llm_file_table(repo_root).get('model_classes'))

Chosen to live in the NEW module, not config.py, for two reasons: config.py has 23 lines of headroom,
and LLMConfig does not need to carry the slots (consumers call load_class_slots directly), which also
keeps the config import edge one-way. _read_llm_file_table (config.py:401) already merges user <
project and already degrades to {} on a malformed core config, so 'a broken pyproject must never
break an LLM op' is INHERITED rather than re-implemented.

Two ACs added and implemented RED-first: the loader reads the sub-table from real config (with a
sibling 'model' key present that must be ignored), and a config with NO model_classes table yields
the documented defaults rather than raising. Mutation-checked: pointing the loader at the wrong
sub-table key ('classes' instead of 'model_classes') fails exactly the integration test.

18/18 unit tests, ruff + mypy clean, module at 197 LOC, config.py still untouched at 777.

compiled_state.description:
# Class config schema and resolver

## Context / Problem
rebar has no way to express "which model for which capability tier". `cfg.model` is a single scalar,
so every per-pass decision is inferred (see the parent's problem statement). Nothing can be wired to
classes until the classes exist and can be resolved.

## Approach
Add three config slots — `trivial`, `standard`, `frontier` — parsed from the EXISTING layered config
(`config.py:388-398`: CLI `-c llm.KEY` > `REBAR_LLM_<KEY>` env > config file > default). Each slot
accepts `model`, `provider`, `endpoint`, and an optional `fallback` array; the array is PARSED and
carried now but not yet consumed (its runtime wiring is a sibling ticket), so the schema does not need
a second migration later.

Expose one resolver: class name -> provider-qualified model string. It reuses `infer_provider`
(`config.py:344`) when `provider` is omitted, so a slot naming only `model = "claude-opus-4-8"` keeps
working exactly as a bare id does today.

Secrets stay env-only: a slot MUST NOT accept an `api_key`, mirroring the existing rule that secrets
are not config-file keys.

**Per-class defaults, when a slot is unset.** The defaults ARE today's values, so an operator who
configures nothing gets byte-identical behaviour to the current release — which is also this work's
rollback story:

| class | default | where it comes from today |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `frontier` | `claude-opus-4-8` | `config.py:39` `DEFAULT_MODEL` |
| `standard` | `claude-sonnet-4-6` | `config.py:45` `VERIFIER_DEFAULT_MODEL`, documented as "the decisive NON-FRONTIER model" |
| `trivial` | `claude-haiku-4-5` | `plan-review.yaml:62-65`, the `model_ladder` entry rung |

Each default is a BARE id, so it resolves through `infer_provider` exactly as it does today. No
default names a provider, so configuring nothing cannot silently pin an operator to one.

**How the flat env layer addresses a structured slot.** `REBAR_LLM_<KEY>` is scalar by construction,
so a nested slot is addressed by FIELD, one env var per field:
`REBAR_LLM_FRONTIER_MODEL`, `REBAR_LLM_FRONTIER_PROVIDER`, `REBAR_LLM_FRONTIER_ENDPOINT`, and the
same for `STANDARD_` and `TRIVIAL_`. This keeps the existing precedence rule intact per key (CLI >
env > config file > default) rather than inventing a merge rule for whole objects.

**The `fallback` sub-object schema.** A fallback entry is a PROVIDER TARGET carrying exactly the same
fields as a class slot, minus `fallback` itself:

| field | required | type | notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `model` | YES | string | a bare id or a provider-qualified one, same as a slot's `model` |
| `provider` | no | string | omitted -> `infer_provider`, identical to slot behaviour |
| `endpoint` | no | string | omitted -> the provider's default endpoint |
| `api_key` | FORBIDDEN | — | rejected loudly, same secrets boundary as the slot |

**It is NON-RECURSIVE**: a fallback entry MUST NOT itself carry a `fallback` key, and one that does is
a typed config error. The chain is already an ordered list, so nesting adds no expressiveness while
introducing cycle risk and an unbounded resolution depth. A slot with no `fallback` key and a slot
with `fallback = []` are the same thing: no fallbacks.

This ticket PARSES and VALIDATES that shape and carries it on the resolved record; CONSUMING it at
runtime is task cc33.

`fallback` is deliberately CONFIG-FILE-ONLY and has no env form, because encoding an array of objects
in a scalar env var would mean inventing a serialization format. An environment needing a fallback
chain uses `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE` — which **does NOT exist yet**; it is delivered by sibling task
cb6f. Until cb6f lands there is no environment-only way to set a fallback chain, and that is accepted:
this ticket's job is the schema, not the delivery mechanism.

**Alternative rejected — a new config file/discovery path.** Forks the precedence chain and duplicates
the loader; the `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE` pointer that cb6f will add is the escape hatch instead.

**THE INTEGRATION POINT — who calls the parser.** `parse_class_slots` takes an already-loaded
mapping, which leaves open who hands it the real config. That entry point is
`model_classes.load_class_slots(repo_root=None)`, in the SAME new module:

    def load_class_slots(repo_root=None) -> dict[str, ClassSlot]:
        from rebar.llm.config import _read_llm_file_table
        return parse_class_slots(_read_llm_file_table(repo_root).get("model_classes"))

`_read_llm_file_table` (`config.py:401`) already returns the merged `[tool.rebar.llm]` table
(user < project) and already degrades to `{}` on a malformed core config, so a broken pyproject
cannot break an LLM op — that failure mode is inherited, not re-invented.

It lives in `model_classes.py`, NOT in `config.py`, for two reasons: config.py has 23 lines of
headroom, and `LLMConfig` does not need to carry the slots — consumers (tasks 172e, 7761, cc33)
call `load_class_slots()` directly. Putting it here also keeps the config import edge one-way.

Without this named entry point the schema would be unreachable from real configuration — a parser
nothing calls. That is what the second plan review correctly blocked on after the scope was
narrowed to keep config.py under its cap.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py` — NEW leaf module: the three slots, the `fallback` entry schema,
  their validation, the resolver, AND the `load_class_slots()` entry point that reads the real
  config table. **Not `config.py`**: that file is at 777 of the 800-LOC hard
  cap (23 lines of headroom) and this schema is far larger than that, so putting it there is not
  landable — the same saturation ticket 1484 just relieved elsewhere. The new module imports
  `infer_provider` / `DEFAULT_MODEL` / `VERIFIER_DEFAULT_MODEL` FROM `config.py` and `config.py` does
  NOT import it back, so the edge is one-way and no cycle is possible.
- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` — only the env-var docstring block for the nine new vars, if the
  generator reads it. Any larger change here means the split above was not respected.
- `tests/unit/` — new tests for parsing and resolution.
- `docs/env-vars.md` — REGENERATED in this change. The nine new per-field env vars
  (`REBAR_LLM_{FRONTIER,STANDARD,TRIVIAL}_{MODEL,PROVIDER,ENDPOINT}`) necessarily appear in the
  generator's output, so the committed file must be updated here or the drift gate fails.

## Testing
Unit tier: pure config parsing and string resolution, no model calls, no network.
- happy path: a slot with model+provider resolves to `provider:model`.
- omitted provider: resolves via `infer_provider`, matching today's bare-id behaviour.
- unset slot: resolves to the documented default for that class.
- a slot carrying `api_key` is REJECTED loudly (the secrets boundary).
- a `fallback` array parses and is carried on the record without being consumed.
- a `fallback` entry is validated to the slot-minus-fallback schema: `api_key` rejected, a nested
  `fallback` rejected, an omitted `provider` inferred.
- `fallback = []` and an absent `fallback` key produce the same resolved record (no fallbacks).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] a test asserts each of the three class names resolves to a provider-qualified model string
- [ ] a test asserts that with NO class configured, `frontier`/`standard`/`trivial` resolve to
      `claude-opus-4-8`/`claude-sonnet-4-6`/`claude-haiku-4-5` respectively — i.e. today's behaviour
      is preserved bit-for-bit when nothing is configured
- [ ] a test asserts `REBAR_LLM_FRONTIER_MODEL` overrides the config-file value for that slot's
      `model` field only, leaving the slot's other fields intact
- [ ] a test asserts a slot omitting `provider` resolves identically to today's bare-id behaviour
- [ ] a test asserts a slot containing `api_key` raises a typed rebar config error naming the secrets rule
- [ ] a test asserts a parsed `fallback` array is carried on the resolved record
- [ ] a test asserts `load_class_slots()` reads the `model_classes` sub-table from the merged
      `[tool.rebar.llm]` config and returns resolved slots — proving the parser is REACHABLE from
      real configuration and not an orphan
- [ ] a test asserts `load_class_slots()` returns the documented defaults when the config file has
      no `model_classes` table at all (the inherited degrade-to-empty path)
- [ ] a test asserts a `fallback` entry carrying `api_key` raises a typed rebar config error (the
      secrets boundary applies to ENTRIES, not only to slots)
- [ ] a test asserts a NESTED `fallback` (an entry itself carrying a `fallback` key) raises a typed
      rebar config error naming the non-recursive rule
- [ ] a test asserts a `fallback` entry omitting `provider` resolves via `infer_provider`, identically
      to a slot that omits it
- [ ] `docs/env-vars.md` is REGENERATED AND COMMITTED in this change, and the regenerated file lists
      all nine `REBAR_LLM_{FRONTIER,STANDARD,TRIVIAL}_{MODEL,PROVIDER,ENDPOINT}` vars; re-running the
      generator afterwards then produces no diff, which is what the drift gate actually checks
